extracted.intended_audience: organisations and program managers considering or managing a Carpentries Partnership (partner contacts, workshop hosts, training coordinators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policies for organisations purchasing and managing a Carpentries Partnership, including workshops, Instructor Training, Instructor Trainer roles, discounts, operational procedures, and partner communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Hands-on, practice-based training in teaching and lesson development; priority access to Instructor Training and Collaborative Lesson Development Training; computational and data skills training via a global network of certified Instructors; professional development in remote collaboration and facilitation; membership in a values-driven community of practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the core benefits Partners should expect to receive and can use to evaluate value against organisational goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Partnership package levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnerships are offered at four levels: Launch, Expand, Scale, and Transform, each with an allotted number of service options that can be used across programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partners may mix and match service offerings regardless of level; choice should align with organisational maturity and goals (see individual package descriptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Launch Partnership suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate for organisations in the early stages of establishing a local community of practice around data science and computational research skills; can be used to demonstrate The Carpentries teaching model as a step toward sustained investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Launch to pilot and demonstrate impact before scaling investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand Partnership suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: For organisations ready to increase training capacity and provide multiple options for skill development and community building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose Expand when you have some local capacity and want to broaden offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale Partnership suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed for organisations seeking to broaden their impact and enable expanded programming for long-lasting institutional capacity growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate for institutions aiming to grow programmes more widely across units or departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform Partnership suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended for organisations pursuing broader institution-wide change, enabling accelerated large-scale capacity growth and sustained organisation-wide impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select Transform for organisation-level strategic, long-term commitments to Carpentries practice and change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom Partnership planning
rubrics_metrics.description: If standard packages do not fit an organisation’s needs, The Carpentries will work with the organisation to create a custom plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact partnership@carpentries.org to discuss goals and build a tailored plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership term and renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Carpentries Partnerships are annual subscriptions that extend for one year and must be renewed each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewing in advance helps avoid lapses in services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount eligibility for contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Discounts on Partnership packages are offered to organisations with members actively contributing in a variety of roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details about available discounts are on the pricing page; contributions should be active and verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to determine if institution already has a Partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of current Partner Organisations is available on the website; contact partnership@carpentries.org for assistance contacting the person in charge of an institutional Partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the public partner list first, then email partnership@carpentries.org for help locating institutional contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onboarding requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the Code of Conduct and join a 30-minute onboarding session with a Core Team member to learn how to maximise the Partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation implies agreement to uphold the Code of Conduct; onboarding provides tips and opportunity to ask questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop types: Centrally-Organised vs Self-Organised
rubrics_metrics.description: Centrally-Organised workshops: The Carpentries WIT recruits Instructors, sets up registration, and provides planning support. Self-Organised workshops: planned independently with certified Instructors; hosts work directly with Instructors; self-organised workshops are free of charge (except AWS/resources for Genomics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose Centrally-Organised when you want Carpentries staff to manage logistics; choose Self-Organised to run locally with your certified Instructors. Refer to Genomics Workshops Terms of Agreement for additional fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrally-Organised workshop operations
rubrics_metrics.description: WIT will work with a designated Partner contact to find Instructors, handle registration, support Instructor logistics, and coordinate and share assessment results with the Partner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor travel expenses are the responsibility of the Partner and are not covered in partnership fees. Centrally-Organised workshops can be purchased a la carte or added to a Partnership and may count toward a Partnership if purchased within 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop curricula coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops can cover curricula from Data Carpentry, Library Carpentry, or Software Carpentry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review available curricula to select lessons that best align with learners’ needs (see curricula page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead time for scheduling workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Partners should choose potential workshop dates at least 10 weeks in advance; generally The Carpentries requires 2–3 months lead time to schedule a workshop to recruit Instructors and allow planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan early to ensure Instructor recruitment and adequate planning time.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request a Centrally-Organised workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the right curriculum, choose dates at least 10 weeks in advance, then complete and submit the Workshop Request Form to initiate the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate audience and scheduling information improves matching and recruitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Organised workshop notification and labeling rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosts must complete the self-organised workshop form so the workshop can be listed and supported; as long as at least one Instructor is Carpentries-certified and one of the core contents is taught, the workshop may be labelled a Carpentries workshop. Self-Organised workshops do not count against Partnership workshop limits and are unlimited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify The Carpentries in advance to receive survey links, tracking, and publicity support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancelling or postponing workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: If cancelling or postponing, inform WIT via workshops@carpentries.org; WIT will remove the workshop from the website and complete administrative tasks. Ensure registrants are notified via email or your registration platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notification helps WIT and registrants; WIT will assist with administrative updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to past workshop survey data
rubrics_metrics.description: WIT can provide survey result links for past workshops (August 2018 - present) to Instructors, hosts, or programmatic Partner contacts upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request by emailing workshops@carpentries.org and include links to the workshop website(s) and/or slugs for identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor Training format and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor Training is a high-engagement, interactive, multi-day training led by pedagogically trained Instructor Trainers. Partners receive a registration code to register trainees for events on the Instructor Training calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trainees may attend as a group or individually; registration codes are provided as part of a Partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting trainees for Instructor Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection is at the Partner Organisation’s discretion. The Carpentries recommends choosing trainees based on enthusiasm and commitment to teaching. No specific technical skills are required; trainees must demonstrate ability to teach one of the lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partners may use the provided application questions to screen candidates if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor Training availability and tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Carpentries offers at least 6–8 online Instructor Training events across timezones during a 12-month Partnership period. Partners are recommended to track trainee completions locally due to privacy and data delays; the Carpentries will respond to information requests within 3–5 business days with available data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local tracking ensures up-to-date records; email instructor.training@carpentries.org for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture of unused benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits, including Instructor Training seats and Workshops, will be forfeited if not used before the end of the subscription period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan usage across the 12-month term; contact partnership@carpentries.org with questions about utilisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchasing additional seats or workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Partners are eligible to purchase additional Instructor Training seats or Centrally-Organised workshops at a discount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See current pricing on the pricing page and contact relevant Carpentries teams to purchase extras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor Training attendance and makeup policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No-shows may request permission to register for an additional event using the same registration code by emailing instructor.training@carpentries.org; requests must be received within 7 days after the end date. Trainees who miss up to 4 hours can schedule a 45-minute 1:1 makeup meeting with The Carpentries Director of Workshops and Training. Trainees who no-show in full without cancelling within 7 days, or who miss part of an event but do not request a makeup within 7 days, are ineligible to register for a new event using the same registration code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the 7-day notification windows and makeup procedures to retain eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor Trainers: role and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor Trainers teach Instructor Training events, training new Instructors in educational psychology and evidence-based teaching practices. Instructor Trainer Training consists of 10 weekly one-hour sessions covering The Carpentries’ teaching philosophy and research underpinning the curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor Trainers are leadership volunteers who also support the broader Instructor Training program; organisations can sponsor participants in Trainer Training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor Trainer discount eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisations supporting Instructor Trainers may be eligible for a 30% discount on their Partnership fee per active Instructor Trainer if that Instructor Trainer has taught at least two Instructor Training events for the global Carpentries community within up to one year before renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discount applies at any Partnership level; eligibility requires documented activity (teaching at least two events). Contact partnership@carpentries.org to request the discount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchasing Instructor Trainer Training seats
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor Trainer Training seats can be added to a Partnership package at any time, either during initial agreement or afterwards; requests are made via partnership@carpentries.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations wishing to develop Instructor Trainers should contact the Partnerships team to add seats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Lesson Development Training description and purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: Training that teaches skills and best practices for designing and developing lessons as open-source projects, using the Carpentries infrastructure, and techniques for effective collaboration and accessibility. To attend, email partnership@carpentries.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This training supports creation of new lessons and onboarding to Carpentries lesson-development workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic Partner contacts and recommended staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic Partner contacts are primary liaisons for an organisation’s Partnership; they receive essential updates and coordinate activities. The Carpentries recommends having at least two Partner Contacts per organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain two contacts to ensure continuity and shared responsibility for Partnership management.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to update Partner Contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Update Partner Contacts by emailing partnership@carpentries.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep contact information current to receive quarterly updates and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership mailing list and quarterly updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic Partner contacts are added to a Partnership mailing list and receive Quarterly Partnership Updates every three months detailing Partnership usage and trainee progress, plus quarterly Partnership Newsletters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these regular communications to monitor engagement and maximise Partnership benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of contact for specific queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated email contacts are provided for different topics: partnership@carpentries.org (general Partnership), workshops@carpentries.org (Workshops), instructor.training@carpentries.org (Instructor Training), curriculum@carpentries.org (Collaborative Lesson Development Training), finance@carpentries.org (legal or financial questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate contact to expedite responses and requests.
